sounds.intro: Tatar (Kazan Tatar) is a Turkic language written in Cyrillic. It has six extra letters, and its vowels follow harmony: front vowels (ә, е, э, и, ө, ү) go with front-vowel endings, back vowels (а, ы, о, у) with back-vowel endings.
notes: Stress usually falls on the last syllable. Tatar has no gender and no word for "the". The verb comes last.
The say column uses simple English-style spelling. "ae" is the sound of "a" in "cat", "ö" and "ü" are as in German.

phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: Tatar has two "you": син (to one friend or child) and сез (to strangers, older people, or several people). Use сез when unsure.

vocab.title: Common verbs
vocab.note: Dictionary form (infinitive). Tatar has no verb "to have": say "минем ... бар" (there is ... with me).

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Tatar has no gender. "Ул" means he, she and it. Use "сез" for one person you respect, and for several people.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: The plural ending is -лар / -ләр (or -нар / -нәр after н, м, ң). It depends on the last vowel: китап → китаплар, өй → өйләр. After a number, the noun stays singular: ике китап.

grammar.title: To be
text: There is no verb "to be" in the present. Add a personal ending to the word: мин студент-мын (I am a student). In the 3rd person there is no ending: ул студент.

grammar.title: Бар / юк: to have
text: Tatar has no "to have". Say "минем ... бар" (I have: of me, there is) or "минем ... юк" (I do not have). The owner is in the genitive: минем, синең, аның, безнең, сезнең, аларның.

grammar.title: Verbs: present tense
text: Take the stem, add -а / -ә (-ый / -и after a vowel), then the personal ending: -м, -сың, (none), -быз, -сыз, -лар. эшлим = I work, эшлисең = you work.

grammar.title: Going: бару
text: The verb бару (to go) is regular. Use the direction ending -га / -гә (to): мәктәпкә барам (I go to school).

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb comes last. Order: subject, object, verb. The adjective comes before the noun.
ex: we live in a big house

grammar.title: Negation
text: Add -ма / -мә to the verb stem: эшләмим (I do not work). With nouns and adjectives use "түгел" (is not) or "юк" (there is none). Always compare with the positive form.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add the question particle -мы / -ме to the word you are asking about: сез арыгансызмы? (are you tired?). Intonation also works.

grammar.title: Possessives
text: Say the owner in the genitive (минем, синең, аның...), then the noun with a possessive ending: минем өем (my house), синең дусларың (your friends).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: Use "син" with friends, family and children. Use "сез" with strangers, older people and teachers, and add "-ыз / -егез" to verbs and nouns.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: add -ды / -де (-ты / -те) and the personal ending: эшләдем (I worked). Future: -ачак / -әчәк: эшләячәкмен.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: use the verb stem (кил! = come!). Make it negative with -ма / -мә (килмә! = do not come!). Formal: add -ыгыз / -егез (килегез!).

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: verb + -а ала (мин йөзә алам). Must: "кирәк" or "тиеш". Want: "теләү" or "-ыйсым килә". Forbidden: "ярамый".
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Tatar uses endings, not prepositions: -да / -дә = in / at; -га / -гә = to; -дан / -дән = from. "Өстендә" = on, "астында" = under, "янында" = next to.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -рак / -рәк for "more": зуррак (bigger). "Иң" = the most: иң зур. "-дан" = than: теге-дән яхшырак.
